providers.title: Linear extensions
providers.scope: Removing a job without remaining predecessors at each step lists a finite partial order in an order extending it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Integer start times suffice
providers.scope: A schedule with real start times on three machines can be replaced by a slot schedule with no larger makespan.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Padding
providers.scope: A deadline T is feasible exactly when the jobs padded with isolated jobs to 3T have a full schedule.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reordering an open interval
providers.scope: Replacing the slots of an open interval by any full schedule of its job set keeps the whole schedule full.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Three-machine scheduling in polynomial time (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A deterministic algorithm decides every deadline and finds a minimum-makespan schedule of unit jobs with precedence constraints on three machines in polynomial time.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The family is polynomial
providers.scope: Boolean formulas of at most K leaves in rank, triple and cone tests describe at most C_K N^(3K) sets, listed in polynomial time.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Soundness
providers.scope: Every set accepted by the dynamic program has a full schedule, assembled along an accepting path of states.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hierarchies give acceptance
providers.scope: If a full schedule has a bounded-description hierarchy, the dynamic program accepts all jobs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Structure theorem (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every full schedule has a bounded-description hierarchy whose descriptions have fewer than 500 leaves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Jobs before a separator
providers.scope: For a separator z at cutoff S and any H agreeing with S on the domain, P_z together with H minus the weak cone of z describes the jobs before z.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No improving exchange
providers.scope: In a normalized schedule, after any reordering strictly after a slot, no job there can be exchanged with a later job of better priority.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One advance
providers.scope: Advancing to the earliest exception keeps every earlier high job below the new slot.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shared-cutoff walk (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Promoting one job, the walk from a separator of the old cutoff ends at a position separating both the old and the new cutoff.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Separators exist
providers.scope: Every cutoff of a set with a full schedule is separated by a slot of some full schedule of the set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cover
providers.scope: Invariant (I1) puts every job of a node in D_a or P_b, in either frame.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Priority orders of the sides
providers.scope: The same and switched priority orders extend precedence, and their promotions end at the center cutoff.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Edge labels
providers.scope: A child's low jobs lie in D_a' and P_b, its high jobs in P_b'; children miss the center.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Suffix carry
providers.scope: A suffix of a list trimmed by a rank threshold selects exactly the qualifiers with key at least the threshold, in the same order.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The new qualifiers
providers.scope: After a same or switched update, the child's qualifiers are exactly its high jobs, and (I1) holds.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: At most five entries
providers.scope: Surviving injections contain different jobs of a three-job slot, so a list has at most five entries.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local flattening
providers.scope: The carried switch pair agrees on later nodes of its run with a two-leaf upset.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short extension
providers.scope: The low set of an existing edge extends to a global downset with at most 21 leaves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The switch upset
providers.scope: A four-factor upset covers the node's X and contains no job at or before its boundary.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: (I2) for children
providers.scope: Every qualifier scheduled at or before a child's left boundary lies in that boundary's weak predecessor cone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: (I3) for children
providers.scope: After any reordering of a child, no key-decreasing exchange with its boundary slot gives a full schedule.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Global child descriptions
providers.scope: A child's high and low jobs are described by bounded formulas on all jobs, without reference to its ancestors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Leaf counts
providers.scope: Node descriptions need at most 257 leaves and split descriptions at most 132.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Running time
providers.scope: With K = 10000 the algorithm runs in O((L+2)^150020) multitape steps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Every fixed number of machines
providers.scope: For every fixed m >= 3 one deterministic algorithm decides a deadline for unit jobs with precedence constraints on m identical machines, returns a schedule, and finds the minimum makespan in time O_m((L+2)^(60m^2+129m+2)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lowering one element of an m-set
providers.scope: Replacing an element of a set of m integers by a smaller integer outside the set lowers every order statistic weakly and one strictly, so the sorted tuple decreases lexicographically.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No improving exchange, m machines
providers.scope: In a lexicographically least schedule of an interval, exchanging a job at a slot with a later job of better priority never gives a full schedule, after any reordering of the later slots.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: At most m injections
providers.scope: A pruned list has at most m injection entries and at most m + 2 entries, because distinct injections are witnessed by distinct jobs of one m-job slot.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Entry sizes and unions
providers.scope: Every list entry has a formula with at most 3m + 7 leaves, and the union of a list or of a carry has one with at most 6m + 9 leaves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Structure theorem on m machines
providers.scope: Every full schedule on m machines has a hierarchy in which every node has a global description of at most 12m + 25 leaves and every mark a relative description of at most 6m + 16 leaves, at every depth.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Correctness
providers.scope: With a leaf budget of at least 12m + 25 the dynamic program accepts the padded jobs exactly when they have a full schedule, and returns one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Running time
providers.scope: For fixed m >= 3 the padded deadline decision takes O_m(N^(60m^2+129m+1)) steps and the minimum makespan O_m((L+2)^(60m^2+129m+2)) steps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
